────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur.. DISCRIMINATING: 'Bacterial_Blight' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on stems vs. angular leaf lesions with yellow halos
Bacterial_Blight: Small, angular, reddish-brown leaf lesions surrounded by a yellow halo, often coalescing into large dead areas; older lesion centers may fall out giving a tattered appearance, starting in the upper canopy on young leaves.
Diaporthe: Characteristic linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems for pod and stem blight, or sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins near nodes in the lower canopy for stem canker; interior of lower stems may show thin black 'zone' lines.
Decision rule  : IF symptoms are primarily on leaves as angular lesions with a distinct yellow halo, THEN suspect Bacterial Blight (Disease A); IF symptoms are on stems with linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) or sunken cankers with reddish margins near nodes, THEN suspect Diaporthe (Disease B).
